coverage_note: The readable opening is the setup of the GATE CSE 1991 Q.3(xii) question, distinguishing a propositional variable (an atomic proposition whose truth value is independent) from a propositional formula (any expression built from variables and connectives). The solution itself was past the cut.
concepts: A propositional variable represents an atomic proposition; its truth value does not depend on any other variable.
Every propositional variable is also a propositional formula, and formulas close under negation, conjunction, disjunction and implication.
The 1991 question gives two tautologies, F1 and F2 implies F3, and F1 and F2 implies not F3, and asks what follows about F1 and F2.
The intended reasoning is that both implications being tautologies forces F1 and F2 to be jointly unsatisfiable.
